Examination Data Privacy Policy

Effective Date: October 1, 2026 | Version: 2.4 | Statutory Governance: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and Information Technology Act, 2000

1. Scope and Objective

This Privacy Policy governs the processing, retention, and security of candidate identity data, response telemetry, and examination audit logs generated across the SSE CBT Examination Platform. This system is administered exclusively for proctored examinations and academic assessments.

2. Data Collected from Candidates

During registration and examination sessions, the platform collects and maintains strictly necessary administrative and assessment records:

  • Identity Records: Full legal name, official registration/hall ticket number, designated branch, email address, and assigned shift/slot code.
  • Terminal and Network Information: Assigned node identifier, local IP address, terminal workstation hardware identifier, and operating environment state.
  • Assessment Records: Question visit timestamps, chosen response indices, review flags, state transition logs, and final submission payloads.
  • Proctoring Telemetry: Periodic candidate video verification frames, focus loss counter, and proctor directive acknowledgments.

3. Purpose of Data Processing

Candidate records are processed solely for the following official purposes:

  • Verifying candidate identity and issuing authorized examination credentials.
  • Ensuring single-terminal session enforcement and preventing simultaneous dual-login attempts.
  • Evaluating assessment responses against verified answer keys to generate deterministic merit ranks and scorecards.
  • Detecting and documenting instances of Unfair Means (UFM) in compliance with institutional examination bylaws.

4. Cloud Database Storage and Security Controls

All data collected is persisted directly to encrypted Supabase PostgreSQL cloud infrastructure with role-based access control (RBAC). Data in transit is secured using Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3). No credentials or responses are stored on unencrypted client storage.

5. Data Retention and Disclosure

Examination audit records, answer logs, and proctoring rosters are retained for the statutory duration mandated by the Examination Board (minimum 12 months following merit list publication). Candidate records are never sold, rented, or transferred to third-party commercial entities. Data may only be shared with authorized academic bodies or statutory regulatory authorities upon official requisition.

6. Contact the Examination Directorate
